display.title: Episode 465: Shoot Holes in the Jacket Too (Shabbos Mevarchim Adar)
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi explains 'when Adar enters, increase in joy', and tells how a tzedakah collector tricked an armed robber into emptying his gun and saved the money for the poor.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week of Shabbos Mevarchim Adar 5751. Uncle Yossi explains that when Adar begins we must not only be happy but add to our simcha, a joy rooted in our trust that Hashem, who never sleeps, protects the Jewish people and foils the plans of every enemy. He prays that this year of wonders will bring a new holiday like Purim and the coming of Moshiach, the king of peace. The Hakochainik march is sung to 'Utzu Eitzah'. A fifth-grade girl from Beis Yaakov of Boro Park leads the Shema, and everyone gives tzedakah. In the story, Reb Nachman, a poor woodcutter who distributes the town's tzedakah, is held up at gunpoint in the forest. Before leaving, he asks the robber to shoot holes in his jacket and hat so the poor will believe him, until the gun is empty. Then he grabs back the bag of tzedakah money and the robber flees. The show ends with a listener's cheerful letter about his whole family, and the neighbors, listening to the program, and with candle-lighting times.
display.lesson: Tzedakah saves from death; treat money given for the poor as a sacred trust, and in Adar add to your joy by trusting Hashem.
